context: Wilde to George Ives, Saturday 8 September 1900, postmarked the 9th, Paris. Two days after the letter asking for £10, thanking him for it. Ten weeks before his death, and the last of the Ives letters here: he asks Ives to bring his friends rather than hide them, and says he constantly reads Edward Carpenter.
quote:
_Saturday_

My dear George,

Many thanks — most kind of you.

I hope you will come over soon — and not alone: but don’t conceal your charming friends — you usually hide them from me:

Your book that you promised me has never arrived — do let me have a copy.

Paris has gone back to summer weather — and the problem of how to dress is acute. One never knows what the day is going to be like.

What a charming book Edward Carpenter’s — ‘Civilization — Cause and Cure’ is — it is most suggestive. I constantly read it.

Ever, with my thanks, yours Oscar
original_provenance: Read at HRC 2700, images 15-16. One folded sheet, three sides used and the fourth blank: image 15 is side 1 alone, image 16 the inner opening, sides 2 and 3. Images 17-18 are the envelope. Emphasis: one underline, the dateline '_Saturday_'. The volume keeps the word and drops the mark. Nothing else is underlined; the stroke below the signature is his paraph. Title, and what the volume does to it: Carpenter's book is in inverted commas in the manuscript and is not underlined - '‘Civilization — Cause and Cure’'. The volume prints it in italic as 'Civilisation, Cause and Cure', which changes the mark (quotes to italic), the spelling (z to s) and the internal punctuation (dash to comma), none of them Wilde's. Taken with the untouched French in p. 1173 and the untouched 'Athenaeum' in p. 1044, this is the clearest case in the set of the volume's single italic standing in for three different things. Read with care: the stroke that appears to underline 'book' on side 2 is the long crossbar of the t of 'that' on the line above, confirmed at 2.9x. Punctuation: his dashes and his colons restored - he ends two sentences on a colon where the volume gives a full stop, including 'you usually hide them from me:'. Envelope (images 17-18): 'Angleterre' underlined, 'George Ives, 93 Park Row, Regents Park, London'; Paris 9 Sept 00 and a London N.W. SP 10 00 receiver; Grand Cafe, 14 Boulevard des Capucines embossed on the flap; docketed by Ives 'Oscar Wilde', underlined.
